items.actClause:
AN ACT establishing the "Gateway Development Commission Act"; and to amend the
civil service law and the transportation law, in relation to facilitating the
creation of the gateway development commission
items.lawCode: Amd §209, Civ Serv L; amd §14-c, Transp L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6372

SPONSOR: COMRIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act establishing the "Gateway Development Commis-
sion Act"; and to amend the civil service law and the transportation
law, in relation to facilitating the creation of the gateway development
commission

 
PURPOSE OF BILL:

To create the gateway development commission, a body corporate and poli-
tic established by the states of New Jersey and New York, to serve the
mutual interests of such states, act as a lead agency for the facili-
tation of the gateway program and maintain itself as an applicant eligi-
ble to apply for and be awarded financial assistance, loans, grants or
other funding as may be available including that awarded by federal
state and local governments and agencies thereof.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS OF BILL:

SECTION 1. PROVIDES THAT THE ACT SHALL BE KNOWN AS THE "GATEWAY DEVELOP-
MENT COMMISSION ACT."

SECTION 2. ESTABLISHES THE GATEWAY DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION TO FACILITATE
THE GATEWAY PROGRAM. THE SECTION DEFINES RELEVANT PROJECTS; ESTABLISHES
A BOARD OF NINE COMMISSIONERS WITH THREE APPOINTMENTS EACH FROM NEW
YORK, NEW JERSEY AND AMTRAK; PROVIDES FOR OFFICERS AND BOARD COMMITTEES;
REQUIRES THE COMMISSION TO ESTABLISH BYLAWS, A CODE OF CONDUCT AND
WHISTLEBLOWER PROTECTIONS; REQUIRES OPEN MEETINGS, ANNUAL REPORTING AND
INDEPENDENT AUDITS; AND PROVIDES THAT THE COMMISSION SHALL BE SUBJECT TO
ARTICLE 8 OF THE NEW YORK LABOR LAW.  THE SECTION ALSO REQUIRES THE
COMMISSION TO ADOPT PROCUREMENT GUIDELINES AND PUTS IN PLACE REQUIRE-
MENTS REGARDING THE CREATION OF SUBSIDIARIES, DISPOSITION OF PROPERTY
AND DISSOLUTION OF THE COMMISSION. FINALLY, THE BILL REQUIRES THE
COMMISSION TO HAVE A TEN-YEAR CAPITAL PLAN AND AN OPERATING BUDGET.

SECTION 3. AMENDS SECTION 209 OF THE LABOR LAW TO ADD THE GATEWAY DEVEL-
OPMENT COMMISSION.

SECTION 4. AMENDS THE TRANSPORTATION LAW TO AUTHORIZE THE COMMISSIONER
OF TRANSPORTATION TO COOPERATE AND CONTRACT WITH THE GATEWAY DEVELOPMENT
COMMISSION TO FACILITATE THE PURPOSES OF THIS SECTION.

SECTION 5. PROVIDES THAT THE APPOINTMENT OF THE NEW YORK COMMISSIONERS
SHALL BE APPOINTED BY THE COMMISSIONER OF THE NEW YORK DEPARTMENT OF
TRANSPORTATION.

SECTION 6. EFFECTIVE DATE.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

THE GATEWAY PROGRAM IS PERHAPS THE MOST IMPORTANT AND URGENT INFRASTRUC-
TURE PROJECT IN THE UNITED STATES. COMPLETION OF THE PROJECT IS ESSEN-
TIAL TO IMPROVE RELIABILITY AND INCREASE CAPACITY ON THE NORTHEAST
CORRIDOR (NEC). THE NEC IS THE MOST UTILIZED PASSENGER RAIL LINE IN THE
COUNTRY, WITH ALMOST 800,000 PASSENGER TRIPS A DAY TRAVELLING ON MORE
THAN 2,000 TRAINS.


THE GATEWAY PROGRAM IS FOCUSED ON THE TEN-MILE STRETCH BETWEEN NEWARK,
NEW' JERSEY AND NEW YORK PENN STATION. THE NEED FOR INCREASED CAPACITY,
AS WELL AS THE DETERIORATION OF THE INFRASTRUCTURE DUE TO AGE, USE, AND
DAMAGE RESULTING FROM SUPERSTORM SANDY MAKES THIS PROJECT ESSENTIAL TO
THE CONTINUING EFFICIENCY AND RELIABILITY OF THE NEC.

CURRENTLY, THE GATEWAY PROGRAM IS OVERSEEN BY THE GATEWAY DEVELOPMENT
CORPORATION, A NEW JERSEY NOT-FOR-PROFIT. THIS BILL WOULD CREATE A
PUBLIC COMMISSION TO OVERSEE THE PROJECT INSTEAD, SO THAT IT WOULD BE
ELIGIBLE TO RECEIVE CERTAIN FEDERAL INFRASTRUCTURE GRANTS.  THESE GRANTS
ARE ESSENTIAL TO FUND A PROJECT ON THE SCALE OF THE GATEWAY PROGRAM.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

NEW BILL.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

UNDETERMINED.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
THIS ACT SHALL TAKE EFFECT IMMEDIATELY; PROVIDED HOWEVER, THAT: (A)
SECTION TWO OF THIS ACT SHALL TAKE EFFECT UPON THE ENACTMENT INTO LAW BY
THE STATE OF NEW JERSEY OF LEGISLATION HAVING AN IDENTICAL EFFECT WITH
THIS ACT, BUT IF THE STATE OF NEW JERSEY SHALL HAVE ALREADY ENACTED SUCH
LEGISLATION, THIS ACT SHALL TAKE EFFECT IMMEDIATELY; PROVIDED THAT THE
STATE OF NEW JERSEY SHALL NOTIFY THE LEGISLATIVE BILL DRAFTING COMMIS-
SION UPON THE OCCURRENCE OF THE ENACTMENT OF THE LEGISLATION PROVIDED
FOR IN THIS ACT IN ORDER THAT THE COMMISSION MAY MAINTAIN AN ACCURATE
AND TIMELY EFFECTIVE DATA BASE OF THE OFFICIAL TEXT OF THE LAWS OF THE
STATE OF NEW YORK IN FURTHERANCE OF EFFECTUATING THE PROVISIONS OF
SECTION 44 OF THE LEGISLATIVE LAW AND SECTION 70-B OF THE PUBLIC OFFI-
CERS LAW; AND (B) THE AMENDMENTS TO SUBDIVISION 5 OF SECTION 209 OF
THE-CIVIL SERVICE LAW MADE BY SECTION THREE OF THIS ACT SHALL NOT AFFECT
THE EXPIRATION OF SUCH SUBDIVISION AND SHALL BE DEEMED TO EXPIRE THERE-
WITH.

AN ACT establishing the "Gateway Development Commission Act"; to amend the

thereof
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6372A              REVISED 06/16/19

SPONSOR: COMRIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act establishing the "Gateway Development Commis-
sion Act"; to amend the transportation law, in relation to creating the
gateway development commission; and providing for the repeal of such
provision upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE OF BILL:

To create the gateway development commission, a body corporate and poli-
tic established by the states of New Jersey and New York, act to facili-
tate the gateway program and maintain itself as an applicant eligible to
apply for and be awarded financial assistance, loans, grants or other
funding as may be available including that awarded by federal state and
local governments and agencies thereof.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS OF BILL:

Section 1. Provides that the act shall be known as the "Gateway Develop-
ment Commission Act."

Section 2. Establishes the Gateway Development Commission to facilitate
the Gateway Program. The section defines relevant projects; establishes
a board of seven commissioners with three appointments each from New
York and New Jersey, and one appointment from Amtrak; provides for offi-
cers; requires the commission to establish bylaws, a code of conduct and
whistleblower protections; requires open meetings, annual reporting and
independent audits; and provides any portion of projects located within
New York shall be designated public work, provided such designation does
not prevent compliance with federal law or requirements for projects or
portions of projects anticipated to be funded by federal funding. The
section also requires the commission to adopt procurement guidelines and
puts in place requirements regarding the creation of subsidiaries,
disposition of property and dissolution of the commission. Finally, the
bill requires the commission to have a ten-year capital plan and an
operating budget.

Section 3. Amends the transportation law to authorize the commissioner
of transportation to cooperate and contract with the Gateway Development
Commission to facilitate the purposes of this section.

Section 4. Authorizes various state and local entities to cooperate with
the commission in effectuating the act.

Section 5. Provides that the appointment of the New York commissioners
shall be appointed by the commissioner of the New York Department of
Transportation.

Section 6. Provides for consent to suits.

Section 7. Provides that the commission shall dissolve upon a joint
determination by the Governors of each state that the project has been
completed or should be transferred.

Section 8. Provides that certain sections of the act may be amended
through the concurring enactment of laws by each state.

Section 9. Severability.
Section 10. Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Gateway Program is perhaps the most important and urgent infrastruc-
ture project in the United States. Completion of the project is essen-
tial to improve reliability and increase capacity on the Northeast
Corridor (NEC). The NEC is the most utilized passenger rail line in the
country, with almost 800,000 passenger trips a day travelling on more
than 2,000 trains.

The Gateway Program is focused on the ten-mile stretch between Newark,
New Jersey and New York Penn Station. The need for increased capacity,
as well as the deterioration of the infrastructure due to age, use, and
damage resulting from Superstorm Sandy makes this project essential to
the continuing efficiency and reliability of the NEC.

Currently, the Gateway Program is overseen by the Gateway Development
Corporation, a New Jersey not-for-profit. This bill would create a
public commission to oversee the project instead, so that it would be
eligible to receive certain federal infrastructure grants.  These grants
are essential to fund a project on the scale of the Gateway Program.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

Undetermined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE
Provides that certain sections shall take effect upon the enactment into
law by the state of New Jersey of legislation having identical effect
with this act, among other provisions.

summary: Establishes the "Gateway Development Commission Act" which enables such commission to facilitate a passenger rail project between Penn Station, Newark, New Jersey and Penn Station, New York, New York.
